matchups.analysis: Both teams are sitting at 0.0 and completely scoreless right now, but ESPN's got this basically locked as Arben's to lose at 52% with a 3.7-point projection edge (115.8 to 112.1)—and that margin holds up because Arben's nine starters are just objectively better built across the board. Rob's entire path to victory needs McCaffrey, Garrett Wilson, and Jayden Daniels all hitting ceiling while Arben's just waiting for Jonathan Taylor, Jaxon Smith-Njigba, and Alvin Kamara to do their normal thing, which is exponentially easier math when you're already ahead in projected value. Neither manager sabotaged their own lineup, but Arben's roster construction is cleaner at every level—he's got the safer floor while Rob's chasing perfection from multiple positions simultaneously, and that gap doesn't usually close when ESPN's already priced in the advantage this tight. Rob could absolutely steal this if everything breaks right, but Arben's positioned to coast while Rob's sweating whether his studs all show up in the same week for once.

Both sitting at 0.0 but ESPN's got this locked as Nori's to lose at 55% with a 9.2-point projection gap (117.6 to 108.4)—Flamur's got nine starters left to play but he's anchoring on CeeDee Lamb, Tee Higgins, and Chase Brown as his only real scorers while Nori's waiting for Jahmyr Gibbs, Brock Bowers, and Deebo Samuel to do literally anything and probably still win. Flamur needs basically ceiling games across the board; Nori just needs his studs to show up and collect paychecks, which is exponentially easier math when you're already spotting someone 9 points in projected value. This technically stays alive with all those starters remaining, but Nori's built to win ugly while Flamur's playing from behind in a matchup where the roster construction advantage is already baked in before a single snap gets played.

Rinor's walking this in at 62% with ESPN projecting a 21-point blowout (115.7 to 94.4), and Ben's nine remaining starters don't matter when he's already getting absolutely buried by a roster that just has better weapons everywhere. Ben's counting on Travis Kelce, Joe Burrow, and Jefferson all hitting ceiling while Rinor's just coasting with Henry, Moore, Adams, and Dak doing their thing—one side needs miracles, the other needs normalcy, and ESPN doesn't usually get that math wrong. This technically stays alive until the final whistle, but Ben's chasing from so far back that his depth would need to produce at an elite level just to make this competitive, and that's not the bet you want to make when you're already spotting someone 21 projected points before Thursday night even starts.

Both teams are sitting at 0.0 and completely scoreless, but ESPN's got this locked as basically a coin flip at 50-50 with Veton sneaking ahead by just 0.6 points (104.4 to 103.7)—which is the kind of projection gap that means absolutely nothing when both of you have nine starters still waiting to play. Veton's roster is just objectively cleaner with Ja'Marr Chase, Malik Nabers, and Brock Purdy as legitimate weapons, while Adam's banking on Puka Nacua, Will Shipley, and Zay Flowers to somehow punch above their weight class against that level of talent—and that's asking a lot when the margins are this razor-thin. Adam needs basically everything to hit ceiling (Cam Skattebo's volume? Flowers' yards?) while Veton just needs his studs to show up and be themselves, which is exponentially easier when you're already slightly ahead on paper. This absolutely stays competitive until the final whistle, but Veton's got the path of least resistance here—his roster doesn't require perfect conditions to cruise across 104, while Adam's sweating whether his mid-tier depth actually delivers or becomes another week of "we were so close."

Rilind and Faton are basically locked in at 51/49 with ESPN projecting a ghost-close 100.5 to 98.4—this is the kind of matchup where your bench actually has to show up instead of just collecting roster spots. Rilind's got the marginally cleaner depth with Amon-Ra and Jeanty as legitimate floor guys, while Faton's leaning harder on James Cook and D'Andre Swift to both hit at the same time, which is objectively riskier when you're already projecting to lose by two points. Neither side sabotaged their own lineup here, so this stays live all the way through, but Rilind's positioned to sleepwalk to 100 while Faton's sweating whether his second-tier guys actually produce or turn this into another week of "we were right there." Both teams have nine starters left to play, so ESPN's edge is basically meaningless—this comes down to whose depth executes, and right now Faton's asking harder questions of his roster than Rilind is.

Jetmir and Peter are staring down a 56% loss probability with ESPN projecting a 10.8-point deficit (107.4 to 96.6) that stays technically alive with nine starters left to play, but this is the kind of gap that doesn't close when Ilir's got Josh Allen, Bijan Robinson, and Chris Olave waiting to pile on while you're banking on Jaylen Waddle and Omarion Hampton to somehow outperform an MVP-caliber QB and elite receiving depth. The brutal part is neither of you sabotaged your own lineup—you just got straight-up outbuilt in the draft by a roster that's legitimately better constructed at every position, which means you can't even blame yourself for the inevitable Thanksgiving conversation where Ilir gets to spend the whole meal reminding you that superior roster construction simply wins football games. This one's still technically alive until the final whistle, but ESPN's got you priced out and your family's got the perfect excuse to roast you all year long when Ilir takes this home.
